subject: Request: GCP Marketplace private offer for CloudSmart — discount escalation
messages:
From: Amir Khan <amir.khan@cloudsmart.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Request: GCP Marketplace private offer — CloudSmart

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at CloudSmart is excited about Redwood's performance and the tradeoffs you showed on batch vs latency. Procurement has asked me to formalize a private offer request so we can accelerate procurement and get co-sell enablement on the GCP side.

High level ask: 40% off list on our initial SKU bundle (see attachments: pricing_model.xlsx). We can commit to a 36-month contract with a $600k committed spend in year 1, annual billing preferred via GCP Marketplace private offer.

Key constraints from procurement:
- The offer must appear as a private offer in the Cloud Console (not a purchase order flow).
- We need reseller/co-sell enablement flags so CloudSmart's GTM team can apply co-sell credits.
- Standard GCP terms are fine but procurement wants a 60-day signature window.

If a 40% list discount is outside of standard marketplace policy, tell me what range you can escalate to. We need an answer by COB PT Monday to stay on schedule for our internal board approval.

Attaching a draft SOW/usage profile.

Thanks,
Amir
Director of Cloud Partnerships
CloudSmart Solutions
attachments: pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet), usage_profile.docx (docx)
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: GCP Marketplace private offer — CloudSmart (escalation)

Team — forwarding CloudSmart's formal private offer request. They asked for 40% off list with a 36-month commitment and $600k Y1. They want billing via the GCP private offer flow and co-sell enablement flags.

Why I'm escalating:
- 40% is above our standard marketplace markdown for self-serve listings.
- This is a strategic partner with meaningful co-sell upside and an enterprise commitment; we should consider a concession if we can protect unit economics.

Attachments: private_offer_draft.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx (attached by requester).

Ask: Can Deal Desk review asap and provide approved discount cap + mandatory guardrails (e.g., minimum ARR, annual uplift, termination fees, co-sell tagging requirements)? Also confirm whether legal needs to change T&Cs for the 36-month term requested or if we should propose 24 months as a counter.

Proposed interim approach: Offer 30% off for a 24-month committed private offer with a minimum $500k first-year spend, and include an uplift clause if usage exceeds forecast. If Deal Desk thinks 30% is too generous, signal the max we can offer and I'll revert to the customer with a counter.

Time sensitivity: They requested an answer by COB Monday (10/19 PT).

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen | Senior Strategic Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: private_offer_draft.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-18T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: GCP Marketplace private offer — CloudSmart (escalation)

Ava — thanks for flagging. Quick read of the numbers: 36 months at 40% is aggressive for a marketplace private offer unless we see clear margin protection via committed billing cadence or non-refundable upfront. A few notes from Deal Desk perspective:

1) Recommended cap: 30% off list for marketplace private offers where Redwood continues to take token-based pricing risk. If procurement insists on 36 months, require a non-refundable 25% upfront on signature + annual true-up.
2) Alternative path: Approve 35% but only for a 24-month term with a 12-month non-refundable minimum (or $300k upfront). That preserves economics and gives the customer a commitment window they want.
3) Co-sell: We'll require co-sell tagging and a joint GCP ISV contact; marketing must confirm co-sell enablement before approving deeper discounts.
4) Legal: No special T&C changes for term length, but include an early-termination charge if they underdeliver on committed spend. I'll loop Legal only if they push past 35%.

Marcus
Director, Deal Desk
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-19T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: GCP Marketplace private offer — CloudSmart (escalation)

Team — after reviewing Marcus' recommendations and the account profile, I approve escalating to Finance for final signoff on a 35% private-offer discount conditioned on: 

- 24-month committed term (preferred) OR 36-month term with 25% non-refundable upfront and annual true-ups.
- Minimum first-year billable commitment of $500k (billing via GCP Marketplace).
- Co-sell enablement confirmation from Partnerships/Channel (cc them once we have terms).
- Early-termination fee equal to 6 months of committed spend if the customer cancels before term.

Ava — please prepare the private offer draft with those guardrails, attach the pricing workbook with the uplift language, and add a line item for the non-refundable deposit if CloudSmart insists on 36 months. Also include an explicit clause that co-sell eligibility requires joint GTM activities within 90 days of signing.

I'll route to Finance and Legal for quick turnaround; push for a decision by 5pm PT today so we can meet CloudSmart's Monday board timeline.

Laura Bennett
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
